solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Picture produced by The Stones?

parts.note: a picture made by setting small coloured stones or tiles in cement; the capitalised Stones pretends to be the rock band

explanation.surface: An image created by the Rolling Stones, perhaps an album cover.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital on 'The Stones' points at the band, but the picture is literally built from small stones.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of artwork is an image assembled from many small pieces of stone, glass or tile.

clue.text: Region south of Ohio has clean bracing air

indicators.note: in a down clue, below means coming after, so the region follows the abbreviation

parts.note: a zone is a region

explanation.surface: An area in the southern part of Ohio has fresh air.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, fresh invigorating seaside air is described by this word, from the gas once thought to be in it.

clue.text: Play along with a group on radio

indicators.note: on radio means heard rather than seen, so the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: a company is a group, as of actors or soldiers

explanation.surface: A band performs on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: A musician who plays a supporting part alongside a soloist is accompanying them.

clue.text: Philosopher seen around quiet uni grounds

indicators.note: around means the philosopher's name surrounds the other letter

parts.note: Albert Camus was a French philosopher and novelist
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A thinker spotted walking around the quiet university grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The site and buildings of a university or college are its grounds.

clue.text: Accept cup of tea needs to be stirred

indicators.note: a cup of tea is stirred with a spoon, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone resigns themselves to the fact that their cuppa needs a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be stirred' shuffles the letters of CUP OF TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: To confront something and come to terms with it is to accept it; the phrasal verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Daft talent night annoyed high steward

indicators.note: annoyed means disturbed or stirred up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An airline crew member was irritated by a silly talent show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'annoyed' shuffles DAFT TALENT NIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabin crew serve passengers aloft, so they are stewards working high in the air.

clue.text: Snobby girl one son found in court

indicators.note: found in means placed inside, so these pieces sit within the abbreviation

parts.note: a lass is a girl
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A stuck-up girl and her son turn up in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone prejudiced on grounds of social rank looks down on others, as a snob does.

clue.text: Posh tenor regularly cut refrain for organs

parts.note: U means upper-class, posh

indicators.note: every other letter of refrain is cut away, leaving its even letters

explanation.surface: An upper-class tenor keeps dropping notes from the refrain of an organ piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Wombs are female reproductive organs; the Latin plural form names more than one.

clue.text: Naughty Pat strips quietly pious people

indicators.note: naughty means misbehaving, so these letters are rearranged out of their proper order

explanation.surface: Mischievous Pat undresses silent monks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naughty' shuffles PAT STRIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: These Cistercian monks are known for their vow of silence, so they are pious and quiet.

clue.text: Bardot comedy about an online business?

indicators.note: the letters sit about, i.e. within, the words Bardot comedy, running across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A film comedy starring Brigitte Bardot about an internet start-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the answer lies within 'Bardot comedy'; it looks like it introduces the film's subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A company trading chiefly over the internet is called this, after the .com web address.

clue.text: It is likely one defies a youth leader

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
to defy someone is to dare them

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of youth

explanation.surface: Someone challenges a young gang leader, as you'd expect.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a mild way of conceding something is probably so, a stock expression of likelihood.

clue.text: Retired vicar having chops and wine

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a vicar's title
chops is slang for the mouth or jaws

explanation.surface: A retired clergyman enjoys lamb chops and a glass of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' looks like a description of the vicar but turns REV back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a fortified white wine flavoured with herbs, used in cocktails such as the martini.

clue.text: Very mean devil with the blue clothing

indicators.note: clothing means covering, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: the blue is a poetic phrase for the sky
an imp is a little devil

explanation.surface: A stingy devil dressed in blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scanty or meagre in quantity, an extreme stinginess, fits very mean.

clue.text: A Stone making a comeback is wicked

indicators.note: coming back means the letters return the other way, read backwards

parts.note: a gem is a precious stone

explanation.surface: A Rolling Stone's return to the stage is terrific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making a comeback' reverses A GEM; 'Stone' pretends to be a band member.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang terms of enthusiastic approval meaning excellent or brilliant.

clue.text: Mate in loo sadly in a tearful state?

definitions.note: a phrase describing a person, matching the adjective

indicators.note: sadly means unhappily, out of sorts, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A friend is crying in the toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' shuffles MATE IN LOO.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone overcome with feeling, close to tears, is moved and upset.

clue.text: No stars and I will play Firestarter

indicators.note: to play here means to be rearranged, the letters performing in a new order

explanation.surface: Without any famous names, I'll perform the Prodigy song Firestarter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will play' shuffles NO STARS and I. Firestarter is a 1996 hit by the Prodigy.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who deliberately sets fires is literally a fire starter, a criminal who commits arson.

clue.text: US reporter from south eaten by puppy?

indicators.note: eaten by means swallowed, so the letter goes inside the other piece

parts.note: a puppy is a young dog, cryptically a new hound

explanation.surface: An American journalist from the south gets bitten by a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'puppy' is clued cryptically as a newly arrived hound.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogged journalist sniffing out stories is called this, mainly in American usage.

clue.text: Winger on fire gets second of goals

parts.note: flaming means on fire

indicators.note: the second letter of the word goals is taken

explanation.surface: A winger in great form scores another goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a footballer; it is a pink wading bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature with wings is a winger cryptically, and this pink bird is one.

clue.text: Language master college caught snorting line

parts.note: a poly is a polytechnic, a type of British college

indicators.note: snorting means taking in, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: got means caught, as in got a cold

explanation.surface: A linguist at college is caught snorting a line of cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: A polytechnic was a British higher-education college, now mostly renamed universities.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fluent in many tongues is a master of languages, so a language master works as a description.

clue.text: Desire one's husband to get behind wife

indicators.note: getting behind puts the latter pieces after the first

parts.note: one is I, plus the 's, giving I followed by S

explanation.surface: Someone wants their husband to support his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get behind' places I'S and H after W.
explanation.definitionFit: A longing or want for something is a synonym of desire, used both as noun and verb.

clue.text: Row about doctor warning of severed palm?

indicators.note: about means around, so the row encloses the other piece

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A dispute about a doctor's warning over a hand cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'severed palm' suggests an injured hand; it is a felled palm tree, and lumberjacks shout this as one falls.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumberjacks shout this word to warn others that a cut tree is about to fall.

clue.text: Win the confidence of underworld member

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and the underworld itself
an arm is a limb, or member, of the body

explanation.surface: A gangster tries to gain the trust of a fellow mobster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underworld' suggests crime but gives Dis, the Roman underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm away someone's hostility or suspicion is to win them over and gain their trust.

clue.text: Foreigner's version of Hello, Goodbye

parts.note: the Hawaiian greeting serves both for hello and for goodbye; Foreigner and Hello, Goodbye pretend to be a band and a Beatles song

explanation.surface: The rock band Foreigner covers the Beatles' Hello, Goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: Foreigner is an Anglo-American rock band and Hello, Goodbye a Beatles single; the word is foreign and means both.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hawaiian word is used as a greeting and a farewell, so it covers both senses.

clue.text: One hammered on ale I hand shot

indicators.note: shot means ruined or broken up, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A drunk, after the ale I hand him and a shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' shuffles ALE I HAND; 'hammered' pretends to mean drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat top of a nail is the part struck by the hammer, so it is the one hammered.

clue.text: Some Cristal costly for Aussie drunks

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A little of that pricey Cristal champagne for some Australian boozers.
explanation.walkthrough: Cristal is an expensive champagne. The definition is Australian slang.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian slang an alco is an alcoholic, so the plural means heavy drinkers there.

clue.text: A reason some won't go out tonight?

definitions.text: A reason some won't go out tonight?

parts.words: A reason some won't go out tonight?
parts.note: going out here means losing consciousness, falling asleep, not leaving the house for an evening out

explanation.surface: An excuse for staying in tonight rather than partying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go out' looks like a night on the town; it means drifting off to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: The inability to fall asleep is the reason some people will lie awake all night.

clue.text: Group withholding recipe for a meal

indicators.note: withholding means holding within, so one piece is kept inside the other

parts.note: a bunch is a group
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin recipe meaning take

explanation.surface: A band refuses to share its recipe for a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a late-morning meal combining breakfast and lunch.

clue.text: Hit enthralling listener is Beat It

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a clout is a hit or blow
the ear is what listens

explanation.surface: A fascinating hit record is Michael Jackson's Beat It.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit' and 'Beat It' look like pop songs; Beat It is a 1983 Michael Jackson hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling someone to leave at once, to get lost, is the slang command of the definition.

clue.text: Half-cut stud during holiday's most naughty

indicators.note: during means within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a rest is a holiday or break

indicators.note: half-cut means one half of the word stud has been chopped away, leaving its back half

explanation.surface: A drunk stud on holiday behaves very badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-cut' looks like British slang for drunk but trims stud to its second half, UD.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of rude, in its sense of impolite or vulgar, means most naughty.
